subject: Why can't the Design tab in the project browser not always be

messages.subject: Why can't the Design tab in the project browser not always be
parts:
Dear all,

In preparation of my fieldwork (with strong focus on estimating elephant
densities) I am 'playing around' with dummy data in Distance in order to
get familiar with the most important features. With some datasets it
appears to be impossible to define a design and run a survey (not only my
dummy datasets, also with e.g. the example =93D4Ducknest=94). I cannot find =
an
explanation for this in the help file.
The dataset I created contains 2 regions with 8 line transects per region
and 15-35 observations (perpendicular distances) per transect.
Have I done something completely wrong, or is there an obvious reason for
not having the possibility to define a new design in some cases?

Martijn Slot

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Why can't the Design tab in the project browser not always be
parts:
Hi Martijn,

The design tab is only activated when the project is geographic -- ie it
contains geographic information. This is because the automated survey design
algorithms require explicit geographic data (the location of the corners of
your study area, etc) entered (or imported) into the built-in GIS.

The best way to set up a project for survey design is to follow the
instructions on the last page of Chapter 6 of the online manual.

However, you can convert a non-geographic project (such as D4Ducknest) to a
geographic one if you want to. Open the project, then click on File | Project
Properties, then on the Geographic tab, and tick the box "Project can contain
geographic information". Set the appropriate projects (or none if none), and
click OK. This now means the project *can* contain geographic information,
but it doesn't contain any yet. (E.g., if you look under the layer properties
for any data layer, you'll see it has no geographic data.) Geographic data is
stored in ESRI shapefile format, and there's no way to add these to the
existing layers using the Distance interface. Instead, you'd need to delete
all the data layers already there and re-create them with associated
shapefiles. Alternatively, shapefiles can be linked in to existing data
layers by mucking around with the Data File (the .mdb in the data folder - see
Appendix - Inside Distance) -- but I wouldn't recommend this for most people.

Hope this helps, and sorry if the manual is unclear,

- Len
